defects.description: The loop `for _ in range(n)` runs one iteration too many (the list already starts with two elements), producing more Fibonacci numbers than requested.
paraphrases: `range(n)` should be `range(n - 1)`; the seed already provides two values.
The loop appends one element too many, so the result is longer than n.
Off-by-one in the loop bound over-generates the sequence.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `range(n - 1)`. Real (list too long), findable via the docstring lengths, distinct.

defects.description: The recurrence subtracts (`fib[-1] - fib[-2]`) instead of adding, so it does not produce Fibonacci numbers.
paraphrases: `fib[-1] - fib[-2]` should be `fib[-1] + fib[-2]`; Fibonacci adds the two previous terms.
Using subtraction breaks the sequence (e.g. it would yield 0 and negatives after 1, 1).
The next term must be the sum, not the difference, of the last two.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `fib[-1] + fib[-2]`. Real (not Fibonacci), findable via the docstring example, distinct from the range defect.

defects.description: For n == 0 the function returns `[]`, but the first 0-indexed Fibonacci number is 0, so it should return `[0]`.
paraphrases: `return []` should be `return [0]`; fib_iterative(0) is documented as [0].
The n == 0 case drops the initial 0.
An empty list is returned where a single-element [0] is expected.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `return [0]`. Real (wrong base case), findable via the docstring (fib_iterative(0) == [0]), distinct.
